name: Acetaminophen
mechanism: Blocks prostaglandin E2 production in the CNS (COX-3). No anti-inflammatory or antiplatelet effect.
pearls: Overdose is hepatotoxic

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI 2.07: 15 mg/kg PO (typical adult 500–1,000 mg), max 1,000 mg single dose
AEMT-C may give 500–1,000 mg IV as an alternative (optional stock)
RI 2.19P: 15 mg/kg PR for febrile seizure if temp ≥100.4

name: Ibuprofen
mechanism: Inhibits COX, stopping prostaglandins that drive pain, inflammation, and fever.
pearls: Avoid in chronic kidney disease: prostaglandins keep the kidney's inflow arterioles open

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI 2.07: 10 mg/kg PO (typical adult 400–800 mg), peds max 800 mg
RI: no NSAIDs in pregnancy, renal failure/transplant, active bleeding, suspected ICH, or possible surgery (open/deformed fractures)

name: Ketorolac
mechanism: Inhibits COX, stopping prostaglandin synthesis.
pearls: Same kidney caution as ibuprofen

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI: Paramedic only. Not in AEMT-C scope

name: Aspirin
mechanism: Irreversibly blocks COX, so platelets can't make thromboxane A2 and stop clumping into a coronary clot.
indications: Chest pain suggestive of ACS / AMI
contraindications: Active bleeding, suspected ICH, or possible surgery (RI 2.07)

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI 3.02: 81 mg × 4 (324 mg) chewed
RI 2.07: 324–650 mg PO for pain; not with active bleeding or possible surgery

name: Fentanyl citrate
mechanism: Synthetic opioid that binds mu receptors in the CNS.
pearls: Little histamine release: less hypotension and bronchospasm than morphine
Rapid IV push can cause chest wall rigidity or apnea

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

conflicts.ri: RI: 0.5–1 mcg/kg, max 50 mcg per dose, 200 mcg total

riPearls: RI 2.07 (AEMT-C): 0.5–1 mcg/kg IV/IM/IN, max 50 mcg per dose
Repeat every 10 min to max 200 mcg adult, 150 mcg cumulative peds
Give IV over 2 minutes; reassess vitals before and 5 min after each dose

name: Albuterol
mechanism: Stimulates beta-2 receptors, relaxing bronchial smooth muscle.
indications: Bronchospasm: asthma, COPD, reactive airway disease
pearls: Some beta-1 spillover can cause chest pain or dysrhythmias
Can be mixed with ipratropium (DuoNeb)

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI: 2.5–5 mg via SVN, ± ipratropium
AEMT-C: up to 3 doses in anaphylaxis

name: Terbutaline
mechanism: Stimulates beta-2 receptors, relaxing bronchial smooth muscle.
indications: Bronchospasm when nebulized treatment fails (second line, IM/SQ)
pearls: Given IM or SQ, not inhaled

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: Not on the RI formulary. Reference only

name: Ipratropium bromide
mechanism: Blocks acetylcholine at lung muscarinic receptors, stopping parasympathetic bronchoconstriction.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to ipratropium, atropine, or alkaloids
pearls: Side effects mostly local: dry mouth, cough
Minimal heart rate effect

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

name: Oxygen
mechanism: Reverses hypoxemia so cells keep running aerobic metabolism.
pearls: Nasal cannula 1–6 L/min
SVN nebulizers run on 6–8 L/min
Supports combustion
Not listed on the RI formulary table; standard at every level

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

name: Lidocaine
mechanism: Blocks fast sodium channels in Phase 0, suppressing automaticity in diseased tissue.
indications: Local anesthetic for IO infusion pain

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

conflicts.nremt: AHA: 1–1.5 mg/kg, then 0.5–0.75 mg/kg, max 3 mg/kg
conflicts.ri: RI: flat 100 mg, repeat every 10 min × 2

riPearls: RI 3.03A: arrest 100 mg IV/IO, repeat every 10 min × 2 (alternative to or after amiodarone)
RI 3.07A: wide complex tachycardia 1–1.5 mg/kg
RI 3.03P: peds arrest 1 mg/kg (max 100 mg)

name: Procainamide
mechanism: Prolongs repolarization and the relative refractory period.

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI: Paramedic only. Not in AEMT-C scope

name: Metoprolol
mechanism: Blocks beta-1 receptors, slowing heart rate and AV node conduction.
indications: Rate control in AFib, flutter, SVT

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI: Paramedic only. Not in AEMT-C scope

name: Amiodarone
mechanism: Blocks potassium channels in Phase 3, prolonging the action potential. Also has Class I, II, and IV effects.

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI 3.03A: arrest 300 mg IV/IO, then 150 mg for refractory VF/VT
RI 3.07A: wide complex tachycardia 150 mg IV over 10 min, may repeat × 1
RI 3.03P: peds arrest 5 mg/kg, may repeat × 2

conflicts.nremt: AHA 2025: 5 mg/kg (max 300 mg), up to 3 doses (max 150 mg after the first)

name: Diltiazem
mechanism: Blocks L-type calcium channels, slowing AV node conduction.
indications: AFib / flutter with rapid ventricular response

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

conflicts.ri: RI: medical control first; max 20 mg, then max 25 mg only if SBP ≥100

riPearls: RI 3.06A: AEMT-C must contact MEDICAL CONTROL first
0.25 mg/kg IV, max 20 mg
If SBP ≥100, may repeat × 1 at 0.35 mg/kg, max 25 mg

name: Nitroglycerin
mechanism: Converts to nitric oxide, dilating veins and arteries. Lowers preload and afterload, so the heart needs less oxygen.
indications: Acute pulmonary edema from heart failure

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

conflicts.nremt: Textbook: SBP >90 in the shock chapter, >100 in the heart failure chapter

riPearls: RI 3.02 (AEMT-C): 0.4 mg SL every 5 min if SBP >100
EMT level: patient's own nitro if SBP ≥100, max 3 doses
No sildenafil/vardenafil in 24 hr or tadalafil in 36 hr
Avoid in right ventricular infarction (preload dependent)
Under 16 yo without known coronary disease: medical control first

name: Furosemide
mechanism: Blocks sodium, chloride, and potassium reabsorption in the loop of Henle, causing rapid diuresis.

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI 3.01: second-tier only
Only if transport ≥30 min, patient already takes oral furosemide, and SBP ≥100
Give the patient's usual daily dose IV, max 80 mg

name: Diazepam
mechanism: Binds the GABA-A receptor, boosting GABA's effect. Chloride channels open more, the neuron hyperpolarizes, and firing is suppressed.
pearls: Strongest muscle relaxant in the class
Only benzo given PR

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI carries diazepam OR lorazepam (interchangeable; service picks)
RI 2.19A: 2.5 mg IV/IN every 5 min, max 10 mg
RI 2.19P: 0.1 mg/kg IN/IV (max 2.5 mg per dose) or 0.5 mg/kg PR (max 20 mg per dose); total max 10 mg
Longest half-life: least desirable benzo when others are available; no IM in peds

name: Lorazepam
mechanism: GABA-A enhancement, as with other benzodiazepines.

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI: first-line anticonvulsant when IV/IO access is available
RI 2.19A: 2 mg IV/IM every 5 min, max 10 mg
RI 2.19P: 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 2 mg per dose), total max 10 mg
Heat-sensitive: expires in 6 weeks unrefrigerated

name: Midazolam
mechanism: GABA-A enhancement, as with other benzodiazepines.
pearls: Fast onset, short duration, causes anterograde amnesia
Preferred IN for seizures without IV access

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

conflicts.ri: RI: 0.1 mg/kg, max 2 mg per dose

riPearls: RI 2.19A: no IV → 2.5–5 mg IM/IN; with IV → 2.5 mg IV/IM/IN every 5 min, max 10 mg
RI 2.19P: 0.1 mg/kg IV/IM/IN (max 2 mg per dose), cumulative max 1 mg/kg
RI 2.25: agitated delirium 2.5–5 mg IV or 5 mg IM/IN, repeat in 10 min if SBP >100, max 10 mg

name: Activated charcoal
mechanism: Carbon matrix that binds toxins in the GI tract.
pearls: Does NOT bind cyanide, lithium, iron, lead, or alcohols
Peds 1 g/kg

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: Not on the RI formulary. Reference only

name: Hydroxocobalamin
mechanism: Binds cyanide to form vitamin B12, which is excreted in urine.

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI 4.18/4.20: if available, 70 mg/kg IV (max 5 g) in 250 mL NS over 15 min; faster in arrest

name: Atropine + pralidoxime
mechanism: Atropine blocks muscarinic sites. Pralidoxime reactivates acetylcholinesterase at nicotinic sites.

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

name: Naloxone
mechanism: Competitively displaces opioids from their receptors.
pearls: Ventilate with a BVM first to avoid a violent sympathetic surge

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI 4.18A: 0.4–4 mg IN or 0.4 mg IV/IM every 3–5 min to adequate ventilation, max 10 mg
RI 4.18P: <20 kg → 0.1 mg/kg (max 2 mg); ≥20 kg → 2 mg IN
Ventilate with a BVM first

name: Dextrose
mechanism: Supplies glucose for ATP production.

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

conflicts.nremt: Textbook: D50 25 g adult; D10 also taught
conflicts.ri: RI: D10 only; adult 250 mL (25 g), peds 5 mL/kg

riPearls: RI carries D10 only (no D50)
Treat when bG ≤60 mg/dL and patient can't take oral glucose
RI 2.10A: D10 250 mL (25 g) IV over 5 min, repeat in 5 min if bG <60
RI 2.10P: D10 5 mL/kg over 5 min, repeat if bG <60
Thiamine 200 mg first if alcohol use or malnourished

name: Glucagon
mechanism: Triggers the liver to break down glycogen into glucose.
indications: Beta-blocker or calcium channel blocker overdose
pearls: Works in beta-blocker OD because it bypasses beta receptors

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI 2.10A: 1 mg IM or 3 mg IN (Baqsimi) if no IV
RI 2.10P: 0.1 mg/kg IM, max 1 mg
RI 2.04A: 1–4 mg IV in anaphylaxis on a beta blocker

name: Sodium bicarbonate
mechanism: Buffers excess hydrogen ions to reverse metabolic acidosis.
pearls: 8.4% = 1 mEq/mL

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: Incompatible with calcium chloride: flush between
RI 2.25: 50 mEq IV if agitated-delirium patient arrests
Incompatible with calcium chloride: flush between

name: Hydrocortisone / methylprednisolone
mechanism: Synthetic glucocorticoids that dampen inflammation and reduce capillary leak.

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

riPearls: RI 2.04A: methylprednisolone 125 mg IV or hydrocortisone 100 mg IV
RI 2.04P: 2 mg/kg IV (methylpred max 60 mg, hydrocortisone max 100 mg)
Onset 1–2 hr: never a substitute for epinephrine

name: Oxymetazoline
mechanism: Stimulates alpha receptors for local vasoconstriction.

source.doc: AEMT & AEMT-Cardiac Drug Classes Study Notes (2025 Guide)

name: Epinephrine
mechanism: Alpha effects constrict vessels; beta effects raise heart rate and contractility and dilate bronchi.

source.doc: RI Statewide EMS Protocols v2026.02 (eff. 6/1/2026)

conflicts.nremt: AHA: 1 mg every 3–5 min, no set max
conflicts.ri: RI: every 5 min, max 5 doses (non-shockable) or 3 (shockable)

conflicts.nremt: AHA 2025: 0.01 mg/kg, max 1 mg, every 3–5 min

riPearls: RI 2.04A: 0.3 mg IM (1 mg/mL) lateral thigh, every 5 min, max 3 doses
Over 50 yo or cardiac history: 0.15 mg
RI 2.04P: 0.15 mg for 15–30 kg, 0.3 mg for >30 kg
RI 3.03A: arrest 1 mg (1 mg/10 mL) IV/IO every 5 min; max 5 doses non-shockable, 3 doses shockable
AEMT (A level) gives IV epi only for non-shockable arrest
RI 3.03P: peds arrest 0.01 mg/kg of 1 mg/10 mL

name: Adenosine
mechanism: Briefly blocks conduction through the AV node, interrupting re-entry circuits.

source.doc: RI Statewide EMS Protocols v2026.02 (eff. 6/1/2026)

conflicts.nremt: AHA: 6 mg rapid IVP, then 12 mg
AHA 2025: 0.1 mg/kg (max 6 mg), then 0.2 mg/kg (max 12 mg)
conflicts.ri: RI 3.06P: 0.2 mg/kg (max 12 mg) first, with medical control

riPearls: RI 3.06A: 12 mg rapid IV push, may repeat × 1
RI 3.07A notes: some patients start at a reduced 6 mg
RI 3.06P: 0.2 mg/kg (max 12 mg) with MEDICAL CONTROL at AEMT-C

name: Atropine sulfate
mechanism: Blocks vagal (acetylcholine) input to the SA and AV nodes, raising heart rate.

source.doc: RI Statewide EMS Protocols v2026.02 (eff. 6/1/2026)

conflicts.nremt: AHA: 1 mg every 3–5 min, max 3 mg
conflicts.ri: RI: 0.5–1 mg every 3–5 min, max 3 mg

riPearls: RI 3.05A: 0.5–1 mg IV every 3–5 min to HR >60, max 3 mg
RI 3.05P: 0.02 mg/kg, min 0.1 mg, max single dose 0.5 mg, may repeat × 1

name: Ondansetron
mechanism: Blocks serotonin receptors in the gut and brainstem vomiting center.

source.doc: RI Statewide EMS Protocols v2026.02 (eff. 6/1/2026)

conflicts.ri: RI: weight bands, 2 mg (10–20 kg) or 4 mg (>20 kg)

riPearls: RI 2.07A: 4 mg PO/SL/IV/IM/ODT, may repeat × 1 in 15 min
RI 2.07P: only >3 months and >10 kg; 10–20 kg → 2 mg, >20 kg → 4 mg (weight bands, not mg/kg)

name: Diphenhydramine
mechanism: Blocks histamine H1 receptors, easing itch, hives, and flushing.

source.doc: RI Statewide EMS Protocols v2026.02 (eff. 6/1/2026)

riPearls: RI 2.04A: 50 mg PO/IV/IM
RI 2.04P: 1 mg/kg (max 50 mg)
Over 65 yo: consider cetirizine 10 mg PO instead
Treats rash and itch only: never replaces epinephrine

name: Thiamine (vitamin B1)
mechanism: Cofactor for glucose metabolism; prevents Wernicke encephalopathy when glucose is given.
indications: Hypoglycemia in patients with alcohol use or malnutrition

source.doc: RI Statewide EMS Protocols v2026.02 (eff. 6/1/2026)

riPearls: RI 2.10A: 200 mg IV/IM before D10
Optional at AEMT, required stock at AEMT-C

name: Calcium chloride 10%
mechanism: Replaces calcium; stabilizes cardiac cell membranes.
indications: Per 3.06A notes, may precede diltiazem depending on BP

source.doc: RI Statewide EMS Protocols v2026.02 (eff. 6/1/2026)

riPearls: RI 4.08: 1 g slow IV, may repeat × 1
Interchangeable with calcium gluconate (service picks)
Incompatible with sodium bicarbonate

name: Nitrous oxide 50/50
mechanism: Self-administered 50% nitrous oxide / 50% oxygen blend for short-acting analgesia.

source.doc: RI Statewide EMS Protocols v2026.02 (eff. 6/1/2026)

riPearls: RI 2.07: optional at every level if the service carries it
